issues.description: Attribute 'lectureName' in class de.tum.cit.ase.Lecture: the problem statement UML and text declare lectureName as a String, but the solution repository declares the Lecture.lectureName field with type LectureName and provides a Lecture constructor that takes a LectureName. Furthermore, the solution's getter/setter are internally inconsistent (getter declared to return String and setter accepts String while the field is LectureName), which causes compilation errors. This mismatch between the specification (lectureName: String) and the concrete type used in the solution — plus the solution's inconsistent accessor signatures — will confuse students and can prevent the code from compiling.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the lectureName type consistent across artifacts and fix the solution's accessor signatures so code compiles and matches the exercise text. Two viable options: (A) Revert to String: change the solution's field to 'private String lectureName;', change the constructor parameter to String, and remove the LectureName helper class; update getLectureName() to return String and setLectureName(String) to assign the field. OR (B) Adopt the LectureName wrapper intentionally: update the problem statement/UML and template to declare lectureName as LectureName and update all solution methods to use LectureName consistently (e.g., public LectureName getLectureName(), public void setLectureName(LectureName)). If you want a String-returning getter while keeping the wrapper, implement public String getLectureName() { return lectureName.toString(); } and ensure the setter/constructor accept LectureName (or provide an overload). Also fix the solution so the getter/setter signatures match the declared field type to eliminate compilation errors.
